content: 1. Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) Availability and Monitoring Sites providing ART should be categorized based on whether they focus on key populations or meet key population sensitization standards. This includes services for preventing mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT). The total number of sites offering ART should be documented, and percentages calculated to determine the proportion of key population-focused sites and mainstream sites meeting sensitization standards that provide ART. Not all sites focusing on key populations are suitable for ART provision, but some may be. When setting targets for ART expansion, it is essential to identify sites with the potential to offer ART and ensure they meet minimum standards. People from key populations must access ART services without fear of stigma or discrimination and receive care from healthcare workers trained to address their specific needs. Ideally, all mainstream services should meet key population sensitization standards. Countries should set ambitious but realistic timeframes for scaling up ART services, considering logistical challenges and resource requirements. 2. HIV Testing and Treatment Coverage The percentage of key populations testing positive for HIV and currently receiving treatment should be monitored. This data can be gathered through integrated bio-behavioral surveys. Not all individuals living with HIV will meet eligibility criteria for ART. Baseline levels should be established through initial surveys, and targets set for increasing treatment coverage over time. UNAIDS has set Fast-Track Targets to end the AIDS epidemic by 2030, including achieving 90-90-90 targets by 2020 and 95-95-95 targets by 2030. These targets aim for 90% of people living with HIV to know their status, 90% of those diagnosed to receive treatment, and 90% of those on treatment to achieve viral suppression. 3. Tuberculosis (TB) Prevention and Management Sites providing TB-related interventions, such as infection control, preventive therapy, screening, and management, should be documented. Percentages of sites offering these services should be calculated. Not all sites focusing on key populations are suitable for TB interventions, but many are. When setting targets, it is necessary to identify sites with the potential to provide these services. Countries should set realistic timeframes for scaling up TB interventions, considering logistical and resource challenges. This includes rolling out TB services to key population-focused programs and training mainstream services to meet key population needs. 4. Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Vaccination Sites providing HBV vaccination to key populations should be documented, including fixed sites and mobile outreach services. Percentages of sites offering HBV vaccination should be calculated. Not all sites focusing on key populations are suitable for HBV vaccination, but many are. Targets should be set for increasing the number of sites providing HBV vaccination over a specific timeframe. The timeframe and targets should be based on logistical assessments and resource requirements for rolling out HBV vaccination services. 5. Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) Services Sites providing SRH services, including screening, counseling, treatment, and referrals for reproductive tract and breast cancers, as well as safe abortion and post-abortion care, should be documented. Percentages of sites offering SRH services to key populations and meeting sensitization standards should be calculated. People from key populations should access SRH services without fear of stigma or discrimination and receive care from trained healthcare workers. All mainstream SRH services should ideally meet key population sensitization standards. Countries should set ambitious but realistic timeframes for scaling up SRH services, considering logistical and resource challenges. 6. Combined Health Sector Interventions Sites providing a defined package of health sector interventions for key populations should be documented. This includes subsets of evidence-based interventions tailored to the needs of key populations. Targets should be set for increasing the number of sites offering these combined interventions over time, with realistic timeframes based on logistical and resource assessments. 7. Data Collection and Target Setting Data sources for all indicators should be clearly defined, including facility-based assessments, program data, and behavioral surveys. Baseline levels should be established through initial surveys, and targets set for increasing service coverage and accessibility. Different time periods may be selected for measuring progress, and countries should document the definitions and methods used for each indicator.
